title: Home screen structure
question: Systems lead the home screen. Choose how they are arranged.

options.label: Era line
options.thesis: Systems stand on a line of release years; moving focus walks through gaming history.
materials: system cards on a year axis
options.viewport: Top two-thirds: system cards placed along a 1977 to 2006 year line, the focused one oxblood with its sun up. Bottom: that system's recent and favourite games as a tile row. Hint bar on the bottom safe edge.
options.risk: Guests who don't know release years may hunt longer for a system than in a plain row.

options.label: Library mosaic
options.lineage: A record shop's crate wall, sized by stock
options.thesis: Every system on one screen at once, each tile sized by how many games it holds.
materials: square-cut tiles on a weighted grid
options.viewport: The whole safe area is a mosaic of system tiles: big for large libraries, small for a handful. The focused tile turns oxblood with its sun; a strip on the right previews its three most recent games.
options.risk: Breaks the fixed 400 x 225 system card into several sizes; small systems get small targets.

options.label: System row and shelves
options.thesis: A row of system cards on top, then shelves of games underneath: recently played, favourites, new additions.
options.viewport: Header with the reversed logo and clock; the system card row first with SNES focused; Recently played and Favourites shelves below; hint bar at the bottom.
options.risk: The most familiar arrangement; Obol's character rests on the cards and the sun alone.
